rows.rationale: The current 143 R0 claims contain no native vision-input or image-cache-key contract. Existing Mac VLM/oMLX packs describe neighboring runtimes. Pinned MLX-LM now has its own processor registry and server image path, so nearby coverage does not close this product-specific surface.

rows.concept: MLX-LM native request cancellation and generation resource lifecycle
rows.rationale: The completed HTTP output defines SSE framing and error timing, but its cancellation claim concerns a downstream wrapper and explicitly leaves native cancellation unresolved. The native worker stop flag, batch removal and sequential stream exit are a distinct end-to-end lifecycle boundary.
rows.delta_scope: Trace client write/disconnect detection into GenerationContext.stop, queued/prefill/decode cancellation checks, batched removal versus sequential stop, generator/cache cleanup and distributed limits. Define code-level cancellation checkpoints; leave timing and recovery claims unverified without a live run.

rows.concept: MLX-LM stateful logits processor rollback during speculative decoding
rows.rationale: The completed sampling claims cover callable order and historical stale-context reports. They leave the current speculative path and external processor state protocol open. Current source provides a distinct composition/correctness boundary beyond stateless sampling options.
rows.delta_scope: Accepted-token history versus rejected drafts, native KV/token-history rewinds versus caller-owned mutable processor state, replay/reset requirements of external FSM processors, and version-specific serial/speculative compatibility. Establish what the code invokes; do not infer that every external processor fails.

rows.concept: MLX-LM distillation loss kernels and custom training loss
rows.rationale: The current R0 configuration claims cover CLI/YAML optimizers schedules and metrics. They do not describe the custom loss callable or KL/JS kernel and differentiation contract. Existing DWQ coverage describes the quantization product, while generic PEFT/compression covers theory.
rows.delta_scope: Library/internal loss ABI, per-position reduction and masking, student-versus-target differentiation, CPU/Metal parity qualification, and how a caller-supplied loss fits trainer.train. Restrict any distillation recipe to what primary code supports; do not advertise a teacher CLI for mlx_lm.lora.

rows.rationale: The existing inference sharding pack and generic 3D/ND parallelism material cover the surrounding theory. Stage-boundary gradients and model/adapter partition mechanics form a distinct adjacent implementation gap.
rows.delta_scope: The external mlx-train reference implementation: PipelineSlice ownership, activation and gradient transfers, scalar surrogate-loss or VJP construction, stage scheduling, and distributed adapter assembly. Explicitly distinguish it from stock mlx_lm.lora and do not generalize its compatibility or speed.

rows.concept: MLX-LM integration contracts for external teacher student distillation
rows.rationale: R1 covers native KL/JS primitives and identifies external orchestration patterns. It does not establish the practical MLX-LM import, logit-vocabulary, tokenization, masking or artifact-consumption contracts used by these external callers. The current tree and installed AI hubs cover generic distillation, not this coupling.
rows.delta_scope: Keep the scope on concrete MLX-LM integration: mlx_lm.load and linear_to_lora_layers use, teacher/student logit dimension checks versus tokenizer identity, student-generated token masks, KL orientation inherited from the native loss concept, offline-SFT handoff, and whether emitted adapter/config files can be consumed by MLX-LM. rows.delta_scope: Only the concrete MLX-LM coupling in mlx-lm-lora and AutoContext: grouped BatchGenerator rollouts and cleanup, sampler/stop-token semantics, reward callback inputs and generated reward module, reference versus trainable model lifetimes, adapter checkpoint interoperability, and exact sequence-ratio configuration. rows.rationale: R1 explicitly found no kernel benchmarks across vocabulary sizes and devices. A controlled performance matrix requires measurement; code and parity tests cannot supply it.

rows.rationale: The R2 open questions ask whether particular runtime/model/adapter combinations preserve probabilities, EOS boundaries and completion masks end to end. Source code can define those contracts, but an executed production compatibility matrix requires measurements. Viability hard gate skips a new source-only research node.
